messages:
Rina S: Quick accessibility check-in — noticed keyboard users lose focus when toggling the right-hand details rail (Model → Metrics → Logs). On tabbing in it's fine, but when switching via the sidebar quick links focus lands unpredictably. Anyone else seeing this?
Carlos M: I saw it too. Looks like the rail doesn't receive focus programmatically and we don't restore the last focused element inside the rail.
Owen P: We should do two things: 1) on open, focus the rail container (tabindex='-1') and then move into the remembered control if present; 2) on close, return focus to the activating control.
Keisha A: Agreed. Also for screen reader users we need clear announcements when sections expand/collapse. aria-expanded on the trigger is fine but some of these triggers are plain icons without accessible names.
Rina S: Example: the compact log-toggle icon only has a title attribute and no aria-label. NVDA doesn't always read that. Let's add aria-labels and role=button where appropriate.
Carlos M: For focus memory I'd store a small map keyed by rail-id with a data-a11y-key attribute on elements we want to restore to. When opening: try querySelector(`[data-a11y-key="${key}"]`) before falling back to the rail heading.
Owen P: Quick code suggestion that keeps things simple:
```
// on blur or focusout
const key = el?.getAttribute('data-a11y-key')
if (key) savedFocus[railId] = key

// on open
const restore = rail.querySelector(`[data-a11y-key="${savedFocus[railId]}"]`) || rail.querySelector('.rail-heading')
restore?.focus()
```
Keisha A: Also check focus styles: our current .btn-icon focus ring is just 1px which fails contrast on dark mode per lighthouse. Need at least 3px visible ring and ensure it meets contrast against backgrounds.
accessibility-bot: ⚠️ Scan results: 3 issues: (1) Low contrast: .badge--muted at 2.8:1, (2) Missing ARIA name on icon buttons, (3) Focus outline thinner than recommended on .btn-icon.
Rina S: For color tokens let's prefer theme-neutral-600 for muted badges (checked ratio 4.6:1 on white). Design can propose token swap and provide hex values.
Carlos M: Another behavioral nit: arrow key handlers on the dashboard card grid are intercepting left/right for paging but cards are not implemented as a composite widget. Either implement roving tabindex or remove keydown handling.
Owen P: Agreed — simpler to remove the arrow key handlers for now and create a follow-up ticket to convert the grid to a proper roving list with aria-activedescendant and arrow support.
Keisha A: For live region messaging — when panels collapse/expand we should surface a brief string like "Metrics panel expanded" in a sr-only aria-live='polite' container. Keep messages short and avoid duplication with aria-expanded.
Rina S: Can someone take ownership for the icon accessibility sweep? We need to audit all icon-only buttons in the console and ensure aria-label + role + keyboard focusability.
Carlos M: I'll take the icon sweep. Planning PR with fixes: add aria-labels, role=button, tabindex=0 where needed. Target Thu.
Owen P: I'll implement focus memory + return focus on close. I'll also add unit tests that simulate keyboard navigation and assert focus restoration. Target Wed.
Keisha A: I'll draft design token swaps for muted badges + focus outline specs and include dark-mode examples. Target Fri.
accessibility-bot: ✅ Note: re-run automated checks after PRs land. I'll post updated results.
Rina S: Thanks team — please link PRs here when ready. I'll do a final NVDA pass on Windows and VoiceOver on Mac after merges.
Carlos M: Linking a quick example of aria pattern for icon-only buttons I used elsewhere: `<button class="icon-btn" aria-label="Open route settings" aria-expanded="false" aria-controls="route-settings-rail">`
Owen P: Also reminder: don't rely on title attributes for accessibility. Use aria-label or visible text.
Keisha A: One more small copy accessibility tweak: status chips read as "ok" or "warn" — let's use full words like "Healthy" / "Degraded" so screen readers convey clear info.
Rina S: Great catch. I'll add that to the UX copy doc. Thanks everyone. :heart:
